title: Outlook: All Accounts view (Unified Inbox) shows email from several accounts in one inbox
summary: The briefing passes: the default, policy controls, licensing statements and rollout dates are supported by Microsoft's documentation and tenant notice. Minor corrections should qualify the no-action and auditing statements and remove the checklist's reference to a control absent from its table.

claims.claim: All Accounts view, also called Unified Inbox, brings email from multiple connected accounts into one inbox view in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: The All-Accounts view, also known as Unified Inbox, lets you see emails from multiple accounts in a single inbox view in the new Outlook for Windows, without merging your mailboxes.

claims.claim: Configuration setting must be Enabled to activate the policy and its default-view and override settings.
claims.quote: Open the policy and set Configuration setting to Enabled. This activates the policy; the additional settings below determine the view and whether users can change it.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; summary
claims.claim: Disabling user override prevents users from changing the configured All Accounts behaviour.
claims.quote: When user override is disabled, the policy controls the view and users can't change the configured behavior.

claims.claim: Enabling the view and disabling override selects and disables the See emails from all your accounts in one place checkbox.
claims.quote: when the unified inbox view is Enabled and user override is Disabled, All Accounts is shown and the See emails from all your accounts in one place checkbox is selected and unavailable.

claims.claim: Users who can override the view can show or hide it from the View tab.
claims.quote: When user override is enabled, users can show or hide All Accounts from the View tab

claims.claim: Users who can override the view can show or hide it under Settings > Mail > Folder pane.
claims.quote: When user override is enabled, users can show or hide All Accounts from the View tab or under Settings > Mail > Folder pane.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Cloud Policy priority resolves conflicting policy settings when a user belongs to several targeted groups.
claims.quote: If the user is a member of multiple Microsoft Entra groups with conflicting policy settings, priority is used to determine which policy setting is applied.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Cloud Policy policies apply only to user objects, not device objects in a group.
claims.quote: Policies only apply to user objects. ... A group might contain both device objects and user objects, but the device objects are ignored.

claims.claim: The policy does not change the offline sync window.
claims.quote: It doesn't change the offline sync window or make locally saved mail a complete copy of every mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The view is an option within new Outlook, whose multiple-account desktop entitlement can be supplied by any signed-in account with desktop-application licence rights.
claims.quote: Beginning from July 2024, Outlook checks the license of all accounts added to the app. Therefore, if any account logged into the app has a license to use the desktop applications, you can add other types of accounts to the app.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: After an account with a qualifying desktop licence is added, secondary accounts can have plans without desktop apps such as Business Basic or E1.
claims.quote: Once you add an account with a qualifying license to Outlook, you can add secondary accounts with licenses for products that don't include the desktop apps such as Business Basic or E1.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence, price or meter specific to All Accounts view, and its policy article names none.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook All Accounts view Unified Inbox licensing price meter Copilot connected accounts data search. Opened Manage All Accounts view, Understand licensing in new Outlook, and the Cloud Policy overview. They give product and policy requirements, not a view-specific licence, price or meter.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy supports most Microsoft 365 subscription plans that include Microsoft 365 Apps, with specific requirements to be checked in licensing documentation.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy supports most Microsoft 365 subscription plans that include Microsoft 365 Apps. Check your licensing documentation for specific requirements.

claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Apps for business, only policy settings related to privacy controls are supported.
claims.quote: You can create a policy configuration for Microsoft 365 Apps for business, but only policy settings related to privacy controls are supported.

claims.claim: With the policy activated, enabling both the view and user override shows All Accounts by default while allowing user changes.
claims.quote: Enabled | Enabled | Show All Accounts by default. Users can change it.

claims.claim: With the policy activated, disabling the view and enabling user override hides All Accounts by default while allowing user changes.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy service is also accessible through Microsoft Intune admin center > Apps > Policy > Policies for Office apps.
claims.quote: Commercial and US Government customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at https://config.office.com or directly in the Microsoft Intune admin center, under Apps > Policy > Policies for Office apps.

claims.fix: Replace the auditing clause with 'when auditing is enabled, Purview auditing records creation, deletion and modification of policy configurations', retaining the condition stated in https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy#microsoft-purview-support.

claims.quote: Set-CASMailbox -Identity <MailboxIdentity> -OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled <$true | $false | $null> ... This example disables Outlook for Windows for the specified user.

claims.claim: Every control that the governance checklist tells readers to check appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: check group membership and policy priority if it differs. The table contains only 'Whether All Accounts view is shown or hidden by default' and 'Whether users can change the configured All Accounts view'.
claims.fix: Remove 'and policy priority' from the After rollout checklist bullet. Keep the documented explanation of priority in Risk assessment; do not add a control row as part of this correction.

claims.claim: The policy article covers new Outlook for Windows, not Outlook on the web or classic Outlook.
